reasons: No tests are visible in this packet.
The rules are strict and well commented, which is good evidence of intent but not proof they work.
Some rules, such as the rule for accepted facts, depend on values set elsewhere.

terms.meaning: A set of rules that data must meet, enforced here by the validation library.
A Python library that checks data types and rules when objects are built.
A fixed list of named choices, such as a set of allowed truth levels.
Where a value came from, such as a source document or an app calculation.
A rectangle that marks where on a page a fact was found, stored as fractions of the page.
A label saying whether a claim is an asset, a material, labour or a catalogue alternative.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module setup and schema version
sections.what: Loads the validation library and the unit check, and sets the schema version to 2.0 that saved evidence files declare.
sections.why: Likely reason: the version lets stored evidence be checked against the format it was written in.
sections.watch_out: Changing the schema version changes what saved files claim to be; older files may need a migration.

sections.name: TruthState
sections.title: How strongly a fact is believed
sections.what: Lists the truth levels a fact can have, such as stated by a source, derived, inferred, typical, rule, corroborated, conflicted or unsupported.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps guesses and calculations visibly separate from values read from documents.
sections.watch_out: A new level also needs matching rules in the validation and reconciliation steps.

sections.name: ConflictStatus
sections.title: Whether facts agree
sections.what: Lists whether a fact has no conflict, is corroborated by another source, is conflicted with another, or has been resolved.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets reviewers and the model see disagreement without guessing.
sections.watch_out: Conflict status and truth level must match each other, and the validation checks this.

sections.name: ReviewStatus
sections.title: Human review state of a fact
sections.what: Lists whether a fact is unreviewed, accepted, rejected or needs review.
sections.why: Likely reason: only facts a person has accepted should be able to drive the model.
sections.watch_out: Accepting a fact means it was faithfully extracted and reviewed, not that it is engineering approved.

sections.name: EvidenceProvenance
sections.title: Where a fact came from
sections.what: Lists the origin of a fact: a source document, a derivation, an inference, a typical value, or a rule.
sections.why: Likely reason: records whether a value was read or produced by the app.
sections.watch_out: Each truth level must pair with one matching origin, and a mismatch makes the record invalid.

sections.name: SourceKind
sections.title: Type of document a fact came from
sections.what: Lists the kinds of source documents the app understands, such as a schedule, plot plan, one-line diagram, equipment list, or image.
sections.why: Likely reason: sets how the location of a fact is checked, since some kinds use pages and others use table regions.
sections.watch_out: Page-based kinds need a page number, and the schedule kind must not have one.

sections.name: ExtractionMethod
sections.title: How a fact was pulled out
sections.what: Lists how a fact was obtained, such as the schedule parser, text layer, table extraction, vector geometry, raster or OCR reading, exact tables, derivation, human review or rule.
sections.why: Likely reason: records the method so reviewers can judge reliability.
sections.watch_out: OCR results can contain reading errors, so the method is kept for reviewers to check.

sections.name: NormalizedBoundingBox
sections.title: Rectangle location on a page
sections.what: Stores a rectangle as four fractions of the page measured from the top-left corner. Rejects values that are not finite numbers, fall outside the page, or have zero width or height.
sections.why: Likely reason: fractions work for any page size.
sections.watch_out: Coordinates must be strictly ordered, so a box that is only a line is rejected.

sections.name: SourceReference
sections.title: Where in the file a fact sits
sections.what: Records the file name, its fingerprint, page or named region, source type and extraction method. Requires either a rectangle or a named region so every fact can be located.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets each fact be traced back to its exact place in its source.
sections.watch_out: The fingerprint must be a 64-character hex code, so any change to the file produces a different link.

sections.name: SourceAuthority
sections.title: How much weight a source carries
sections.what: Lists the authority of a source, such as issued project information, conceptual design, estimate, standard options, vendor go-by, design study, reference manual or schedule export.
sections.why: Likely reason: prevents weaker sources from driving model geometry.
sections.watch_out: Standard and vendor sources only count for model use when tied to a specific asset.

sections.name: Applicability
sections.title: Which project or asset a fact applies to
sections.what: Lists whether a fact is unresolved, explicitly for this project, explicitly for one asset, a general reference, or for another project.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops facts from one project from being used on another.
sections.watch_out: Only facts tied to this project or a specific asset can drive the model.

sections.name: ClaimContext (part 1)
sections.title: Claim fields and their meaning
sections.what: Describes one claimed value with its subject, project, applicability, authority, raw and normalized values and units, revision, option, design status and quantity role.
sections.why: Stated in the code: the docstring says acceptance is not engineering approval and normalization grants no design authority.
sections.watch_out: Default values such as unselected option and not-a-quantity change how a claim is used, so check them when a claim seems to be ignored.

sections.name: ClaimContext: validate_context
sections.title: Claim consistency checks and model permission
sections.what: Checks option status, finite numbers, allowed design status and quantity role, and requires a project identity and source basis for project or asset claims. Also decides whether a claim may feed the model, based on applicability, authority, option, design status and quantity role, and whether its unit fits the fact type.
sections.why: Likely reason: rejects contradictory claims before they reach the model, and keeps design decisions with the model rather than the claim.
sections.watch_out: A selected option needs both an option name and a source basis, and a missing value on either side fails validation.

sections.name: EvidenceRecord (part 1)
sections.title: Single fact record fields and checks
sections.what: Defines one evidence fact with its ID, type, subject, value, unit, source, confidence, review state, truth state and notes. Checks that the claim value matches the shared value and unit, and that reference lists contain no duplicates.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps each fact consistent with itself before it is stored.
sections.watch_out: A fact cannot both corroborate and conflict with the same other fact, and this check runs here.

sections.name: EvidenceRecord (part 2)
sections.title: Truth, review and provenance rules
sections.what: Checks that corroborated, conflicted and unsupported truth agree with their status fields, that an accepted fact is not in conflict, and that origin matches truth level. Also defines whether a reviewed fact may drive the model.
sections.why: Likely reason: one gate that blocks contested, unsupported or unpermitted facts from the model.
sections.watch_out: A fact with a claim is blocked from the model when that claim does not permit model use, even if the fact is accepted.

sections.name: EvidenceBundle
sections.title: Collection of facts for one scope
sections.what: Holds the evidence records for one scope, checks that fact IDs are unique and that every reference points to a fact in the same bundle, and offers lookups by ID and a list of accepted facts.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes sure the whole set of facts is internally consistent.
sections.watch_out: A single fact that cites a missing ID makes the whole bundle invalid.

summary: Defines the shape and rules of every evidence fact, claim and bundle, so that a fact that breaks the rules is rejected when it is created.
purpose: Keeps each fact traceable to its source, its truth level, its review state and its permission to affect the model.
why: Likely reason: the header says these contracts are shared by every output, so one strict definition keeps all outputs consistent. The docstrings state that acceptance means faithful extraction, not engineering approval.
how: 1. Defines the allowed values for truth, conflict, review, provenance, source type, extraction method and authority. 2. Defines the source location, including a bounding box and page or region rules. 3. Defines the claim context, which records who the value applies to, its authority, units, revision and option, and checks those rules. 4. Defines the evidence record and checks that its truth, conflict, review and provenance fields agree. 5. Defines the bundle, which checks fact IDs are unique and that references point to existing facts. 6. Provides helper checks that decide whether a claim or fact may drive the model.
inputs: Field values from callers or from stored data, checked by the validation rules as the objects are created.
outputs: Validated Python objects for facts, claims, sources and bundles. Invalid combinations raise errors instead of being stored.
risks: Many rules interact: a fact can only be accepted if it is not conflicted, not unsupported and, when it has a claim, that claim permits model use. Changing one enum value can silently break saved data. A fact with a claim must repeat its raw value and unit exactly.
debug: When a record is rejected, read the error text, which names the broken rule. Check that truth state and provenance match, that conflict status matches truth state, and that every referenced fact ID exists in the same bundle. For a claim ignored by the model, check its applicability, authority, option status and quantity role.
